audience.text: Developers building or converting 3D scenes in Node.js environments who need a pure TypeScript API compatible with Aspose.3D.

capabilities.text: Construct hierarchical 3D scenes using Scene, Node, and Entity types with support for child nodes, transforms, and optional geometry.
capabilities.title: Scene graph construction

capabilities.text: Create mesh geometry with control points, polygons, and vertex attribute channels including normals, UVs, and vertex colors.
capabilities.title: Mesh geometry creation

capabilities.text: Assign shading materials including LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, and PbrMaterial with texture mapping support.
capabilities.title: Material assignment

capabilities.text: Add Camera and Light entities to scenes with configurable projection types, field of view, clip planes, and light types.
capabilities.title: Camera and light entities

capabilities.text: Animate node properties using keyframe sequences with configurable interpolation, extrapolation, and binding points.
capabilities.title: Animation support

capabilities.text: Read and write interchange formats including glTF, OBJ, STL, FBX, and COLLADA through dedicated import/export paths.
capabilities.title: Format I/O

capabilities.text: Perform 2D/3D/4D vector operations, matrix transformations, quaternion math, and geometric utilities like ray intersection and triangle containment.
capabilities.title: Math utilities

capabilities.text: Manage metadata and custom properties on scene objects using the Property and PropertyCollection APIs.
capabilities.title: Property system

limitations.text: Rendering is not implemented — Scene.render() throws an error.
Boolean operations on Mesh (union, difference, intersect), optimize(), and isManifold() throw 'not implemented' errors.
VertexElement.setIndices() and clear() throw 'not implemented' errors.
Node.selectSingleObject() and selectObjects() throw 'not implemented' errors.
FileSystem virtualization abstraction methods (readFile, writeFile, createZipFileSystem, etc.) are unimplemented and throw errors.
OBJ export only writes geometry attached at the top of the scene graph; child-node-attached geometry is silently omitted.

problems_solved.text: Enables construction of 3D scenes with hierarchical scene graphs, mesh geometry, materials, cameras, and lights using a TypeScript API.
Supports reading and writing common 3D interchange formats such as glTF, OBJ, STL, FBX, and COLLADA.
Provides animation support through keyframe sequences, animation clips, and interpolation/extrapolation controls.
Offers utilities for mesh triangulation, bounding box calculations, and vector/matrix math operations.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for TypeScript is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed TypeScript/JavaScript library for building and converting 3D scenes in Node.js.

uncertainties: OBJ import does not currently assign per-face materials from the source file regardless of load option value — confirmed by direct testing against a real fixture.
Binary GLB export currently fails for any non-empty mesh; JSON/ASCII form is unaffected. Binary GLB import is unaffected either way.
Re-importing a scene this library exported to glTF can come back with extra, duplicate top-level nodes not present in the original.
Text watermarking is not currently functional in this FOSS build (the identical defect independently confirmed on the sibling 3d/net platform).
A real npm packaging defect affects 3MF import/export in this FOSS build — a normal package install does not pull in a dependency the 3MF code path needs at runtime.
A real npm packaging defect affects this package's declared entry point — the real build does not produce the file package.json points consumers at.
The inherited README states OBJ export carries 'real, current defects' but does not specify whether these affect all OBJ export or only specific configurations.
The inherited README states 'Mesh' height-map constructor path is not implemented but no public symbol for such a constructor is present in the fact dossier.

workflows.name: Load and save 3D scenes
workflows.text: Load a scene from a file or buffer using Scene.open() or Scene.openFromBuffer(), then save it to another format using Scene.save() or Scene.saveToBuffer().

workflows.name: Build mesh geometry
workflows.text: Create a Mesh, add control points, and define polygons using Mesh.addControlPoint() and Mesh.createPolygon(), then attach vertex attribute channels.

workflows.name: Assign materials
workflows.text: Instantiate material subclasses such as LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial and assign them to scene nodes.

workflows.name: Animate node properties
workflows.text: Create AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and AnimationChannel objects, populate KeyframeSequence with KeyFrame instances, and attach them to the scene.

workflows.name: Triangulate geometry
workflows.text: Use PolygonModifier.triangulate() on raw control points or call Mesh.triangulate() to triangulate an existing mesh's polygons in place.

workflows.name: Inspect scene hierarchy
workflows.text: Traverse the scene graph using Scene.rootNode, Node.childNodes, Node.entities, and related properties to inspect or modify the structure.
